pages.headline: Nifty rose, but smaller stocks fell
pages.lead: In October 2026, Nifty 50 gained 1.95%, but Nifty 500 fell 0.75%, Midcap 150 fell 3.69% and Smallcap 250 fell 5.78%. These are index returns, not individual share prices.
analysis: The Nifty 50 did better than the wider Nifty 500 by 2.70 percentage points. A rise in the headline index did not mean most shares were rising.
The RBI increased its repo rate to 5.50% in October. Consumer inflation (CPI) was 6.09% year on year, so borrowing costs and company profits need closer attention.
pages.risk_note: These are October's completed-month figures. They do not tell us where the market will go in November or which share to buy.

pages.headline: Inflation and RBI rates: what changed?
pages.lead: India's consumer inflation (CPI) was 6.09% in October 2026, and food prices rose 8.94% from a year earlier. Industrial output (IIP) grew 6.7% in September.
analysis: The RBI raised the repo rate from 5.25% to 5.50%. That is a 0.25 percentage-point rise, or 25 basis points (bps), not a 25% increase.
CPI tracks the rise in consumer prices. IIP tracks factory and industrial output. The figures cover different months and should not be compared as if they measure the same thing.
pages.risk_note: The inflation and industrial-output figures may be revised. These changes do not guarantee that Nifty or any particular share will rise or fall.

pages.headline: Nifty 50: one good month, a weaker year
pages.lead: NSE Indices reports Nifty 50 total returns of +1.95% for one month, -5.29% for three months and -9.45% for one year as of 31 October 2026.
analysis: The index P/E (price-to-earnings ratio) was 19.30, its price-to-book ratio was 2.83, and its reported one-year volatility was 13.90%. These are market-wide measures.
One positive month does not prove that the longer-term trend has turned. Check the time period of each return before drawing a conclusion.
pages.risk_note: These are total returns, which include dividends under the index method. They are not daily price candles, support levels or buy/sell signals.

pages.headline: Bank Nifty held steady while mid and small caps fell
pages.lead: In October, Nifty Bank gained just 0.10%. Nifty 50 gained 1.95%, while Nifty 500 fell 0.75%, Midcap 150 fell 3.69% and Smallcap 250 fell 5.78%.
analysis: Bank Nifty's P/E was 12.23 against Nifty 50's 19.30. This is not enough to say banks are cheap: the two indices contain different types of businesses.
The main lesson: when Nifty 50 rises, banking, mid-cap and small-cap shares may still move differently. Compare each index using the same dated source.
pages.risk_note: Index returns do not identify a winning bank or stock. These figures are total returns from NSE Indices, not verified live trading prices.

pages.headline: Are most shares rising? Look beyond Nifty 50
pages.lead: The Nifty 500 fell 0.75% in October, but its equal-weight version fell 5.12%. The gap was 4.37 percentage points on the same NSE Indices dashboard.
analysis: An equal-weight index gives each company a similar weight, while a market-cap-weighted index gives bigger companies more influence. The difference suggests uneven performance.
We do not yet have source-checked numbers for rising versus falling shares or for foreign and domestic institutional buying (FII/DII flows). Those figures are not shown.
pages.risk_note: This comparison hints at market concentration; it is not an official advance-decline count. We have deliberately left unverified FII/DII flows out.

pages.headline: IT led the sectors; metals and capital goods fell
pages.lead: In October, the Nifty IT sector index gained 18.06%, Pharma gained 2.60%, PSU Bank gained 2.73%, while the Nifty Metal index fell 7.51%.
analysis: Capital Goods fell 7.23% and Auto fell 3.31%; the Healthcare index rose 1.93%. These are sector-index returns for October, not returns of individual shares.
Different sectors moved in different directions. To explain why a specific share moved, its earnings, company announcements and valuation must be checked separately.
pages.risk_note: A strong sector return does not mean every share in that sector performed well. Sector indices can have different company mixes and calculation rules.

pages.headline: Large caps: what Nifty 50 valuations tell us
pages.lead: On 31 October, Nifty 50 had a P/E (price-to-earnings ratio) of 19.30, a price-to-book ratio of 2.83 and a dividend yield of 1.42%.
analysis: NSE Indices reported one-year volatility of 13.90% for Nifty 50 and an October total return of +1.95%. Volatility indicates how much returns can vary.
TCS reported consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue of Rs 73,188 crore in its NSE filing. This is company revenue in Indian rupees, not a stock recommendation.
pages.risk_note: TCS is included as a research example only. A sound share valuation also needs the latest share price, profit, debt and other verified accounts.

pages.headline: Mid caps: returns and valuations need care
pages.lead: Nifty Midcap 150 fell 3.69% in October. Its P/E (price-to-earnings ratio) was 26.27 and its one-year volatility was 16.75% as of 31 October.
analysis: Midcap 150's P/E was 6.97 higher than Nifty 50's 19.30. That does not automatically mean it is overpriced; company growth and profits must be studied too.
Persistent Systems reported Q2 FY27 revenue of $487.6 million, up 20.0% from a year earlier in US dollars, and a 15.0% EBIT operating margin.
pages.risk_note: Persistent is shown as a company research example, not as a verified Midcap 150 constituent or a recommendation to buy its shares.

pages.headline: Small caps: higher valuations, bigger risks
pages.lead: Nifty Smallcap 250 fell 5.78% in October. Its P/E was 31.28 and its one-year volatility was 18.14% on the official NSE Indices dashboard.
analysis: Compared with Nifty 50, the Smallcap 250 index had both a higher P/E and higher measured volatility. Its October loss was also bigger.
Before selecting a small-cap share, check trading liquidity, company debt, cash generated by the business and whether profits are improving.
pages.risk_note: These are index-wide numbers, not a ranking of individual small-cap shares. We are not presenting an unverified top-five stock list.

pages.headline: TCS, Persistent and Coforge: compare carefully
pages.lead: TCS reported Q2 FY27 revenue of Rs 73,188 crore in Indian rupees. Persistent and Coforge reported US-dollar revenue growth of 20.0% and 40.1% respectively.
analysis: TCS reports the figure here in rupees, while the other two growth figures use US dollars. We exclude TCS from the USD growth chart rather than make an unfair comparison.
Persistent reported USD revenue of $487.6 million; Coforge reported $652.2 million. Their business mix and acquisition effects also need separate checks.
pages.risk_note: Three companies using different reporting bases cannot be ranked fairly from these numbers alone. This page is research, not a buy list.

pages.headline: Market strategy: two inflation scenarios
pages.lead: The observed figures were RBI repo rate 5.50%, consumer inflation (CPI) 6.09%, Nifty 50 October return +1.95% and Smallcap 250 return -5.78%.
analysis: If inflation stays high, borrowing could remain expensive for companies. Investors should look more closely at interest costs and working capital in company accounts.
If inflation eases, some cost pressure may reduce. That alone cannot predict a share-price rise: company profits and valuation still matter.
pages.risk_note: These are possible situations for learning, not forecasts. They do not give a future return, target price or intraday trading entry.

pages.headline: Market calendar: important dates to watch
pages.lead: MoSPI's release calendar scheduled October IIP for 28 November and Q2 FY27 GDP for 30 November.
analysis: The RBI Monetary Policy Committee meeting was scheduled for 2–4 December 2026.
November CPI was scheduled for 14 December, or the next working day if the date is a holiday.
pages.risk_note: Release dates can change. Check RBI and government announcements again before acting on a calendar item or publishing a new issue.

pages.headline: Next-month watchlist: avoid false confidence
pages.lead: Nifty 50 gained 1.95% in October, while Nifty 500 fell 0.75%, Midcap 150 fell 3.69% and Smallcap 250 fell 5.78%. The market was not rising evenly.
analysis: Before investing in a company, compare cash flow, debt, liquidity and profit changes using accounts from the same reporting period.
Watch whether gains spread beyond large companies. Review the latest GDP, inflation and RBI updates before changing a market view.
pages.risk_note: These observations do not set a model portfolio, target return, index level or buy/sell price for any retail investor.

pages.headline: How we check numbers and explain risks
pages.lead: Index figures in this draft come from NSE Indices' October 2026 dashboard. Inflation, industrial output and RBI repo-rate figures use dated official releases.
analysis: TCS's Q2 revenue in rupees comes from its NSE filing. Persistent and Coforge's US-dollar figures are based on their own quarterly results.
Each number needs a date, units and a source. A website link alone is not enough: we also check the saved source document and require human review.
pages.risk_note: This magazine is general market research, not personal financial advice. Release requires visual, source, editorial and Telegram delivery checks.

reader_profile.policy: Use Nifty, RBI, share, Rs and crore; define jargon once, use period+unit for every metric; never turn index returns into recommendations
